fault: The {KEY} key on your keyboard does not register when pressed.
diagnosis: A dead key on a hot-swap board usually means a faulty switch or a dirty socket. I'll unplug the keyboard, swap the {KEY} switch for a spare, and test it.
safety_notes: Unplug the USB-C cable before pulling any switch.
Touch grounded metal or wear an anti-static strap before handling the board.
Never rock or yank a switch; it can damage the hot-swap socket.

steps.title: Unplug the keyboard
steps.instruction: Unplug the USB-C cable from the back of the keyboard. Touch grounded metal first.
steps.expected_visual_state: No cable is in the USB-C port and the backlight is off.
common_mistakes: Leaving the cable plugged in while pulling switches.
Reaching for the board without grounding yourself first.

steps.title: Remove the keycap
steps.instruction: Hook the keycap puller under opposite edges of the {KEY} keycap and pull straight up. Set the keycap aside.
steps.expected_visual_state: The {KEY} keycap is off and the bare switch is visible in the plate.
common_mistakes: Pulling the wrong keycap.
Pulling at an angle, which stresses the stem or scratches the case.

steps.title: Place the switch puller
steps.instruction: Put the switch puller prongs on the top and bottom clips of the {KEY} switch, down at plate level.
steps.expected_visual_state: The switch puller prongs rest on the top and bottom edges of the {KEY} switch, not the sides.
common_mistakes: Gripping the left and right sides so the switch won't release.
Placing the prongs high on the housing instead of at plate level.

steps.title: Pull the switch out
steps.instruction: Squeeze gently until the clips give, then pull the {KEY} switch straight up.
steps.expected_visual_state: The old switch is in the puller and an empty hole shows the socket below.
common_mistakes: Rocking the switch sideways, which damages the socket.
Pulling at an angle instead of vertically.

steps.title: Clean the socket
steps.instruction: Look into the empty {KEY} hole and blow it clean with compressed air.
steps.expected_visual_state: The socket's two pin holes are visible, free of debris, and the socket is not lifted or damaged.
common_mistakes: Missing a damaged or lifted socket.
Inserting the new switch over debris.

steps.title: Check the spare switch
steps.instruction: Hold up the spare switch and check both pins are straight. Straighten a bent pin gently with tweezers.
steps.expected_visual_state: The spare switch shows two straight, parallel pins pointing down.
common_mistakes: Installing a switch with a bent pin.
Bending a pin too hard and snapping it.

steps.title: Align the spare switch
steps.instruction: Hold the spare switch over the {KEY} hole, facing like its neighbours. Line the pins up with the socket holes.
steps.expected_visual_state: The spare switch sits level over the hole, oriented like its neighbours, not yet pressed in.
common_mistakes: Rotating the switch so the pins miss the holes.
Holding it tilted so one pin enters first.

steps.title: Press the switch in
steps.instruction: Press straight down on the top of the switch until it clicks flush.
steps.expected_visual_state: The new switch sits flush in the plate at the same height as its neighbours.
common_mistakes: Forcing a switch with crooked pins.
Pressing one corner only so it seats crooked.

steps.title: Replace the keycap
steps.instruction: Line the {KEY} keycap up with the stem and press it straight down until seated.
steps.expected_visual_state: The {KEY} keycap is on at the same height and angle as its neighbours.
common_mistakes: Putting the keycap on rotated.
Not seating it fully so it sits high.

steps.title: Reconnect and test
steps.instruction: Plug the USB-C cable back in. Press the {KEY} key three times in a text editor.
steps.expected_visual_state: The cable is plugged in, the backlight is on, and the {KEY} character appears once per press.
common_mistakes: Not testing the specific repaired key.
Not checking for double-typing.
